Correction to the auditor: spend $75K with goal $22,100 at 27.6% is about 155px at 1280 and fits; it clips only at about 320px.

open.dynamic: Scenario 'capped' (DevResults.jsx:165: q2=270000, q7=4000, q8=400, q11=62500, plg). Node: currentRPV 5.625 ($5.63); goal 36.875 ($36.88); ceilingRPV = (48000×0.6×50 + 207500)/48000 = 34.32 < 12×5.625, so maxRPV is 34.32. The goal is beyond maxRPV, gain is $1,377,500 and the gap is $122,500, which gives Block 5 (capped). Opt-in is 10% and RPS $13.02, both red, so the headline renders "toward $36.88 and add $125K/month…" above Block 5's "still $122,500 short".

open.evidence: TheCatch.jsx:111-115 focusProps = { onMouseEnter: setFocus(i), onMouseLeave: setFocus(null), onClick: setFocus(f => f === i ? null : i) }; :216-220 bubble only when focus === i; package.json react ^18.3.1
open.detail: Traced through React 18 event handling. On a touch tap, Chrome fires compatibility mouseover (React onMouseEnter, focus = i) and then click. The toggle sees f === i and sets null. React keeps update order, so the final state is null: the first tap on any pillar only flashes. Tapping a different pillar repeats this, and only a second tap on the same pillar sticks. The same handler also hurts desktop: clicking a pillar you are already hovering clears its highlight and bubble. iOS Safari may suppress the click after a hover change, so it could work there. This comes from reading the code; it has not been seen in a browser.
open.suggested_fix: Use onPointerEnter/onPointerLeave guarded by e.pointerType === 'mouse' for hover. Make onClick a toggle only for non-mouse pointers (remember the last pointerType), or have it set focus to i without toggling for mouse. Check in mobile emulation with touch at 375px on ?results=fixture: one tap on PILLAR 02's total should keep the highlight and the bubble.

all.evidence: AdSpendSection.jsx:73-74 ('const inside = w >= 30 || after > 78;'), 153-155; AdSpendSection.css:294-308 (.rad__bar: overflow:hidden, justify-content:flex-end, padding 0 10px)
all.detail: When the dashed spend line sits past 78% of the scale, the label is forced inside the bar however narrow the bar is. The flex-end content then overflows to the left and overflow:hidden cuts it. Estimated from font metrics, a clipped label occurs in 60 of the 900 ad combos at 1280 (30 at the under-$10k tier, 24 at $270K, 6 at $810K), 54 at 768, 66 at 375 and 216 at 320. At 320, 'w ≥ 30' bars are also often too narrow for 7-8 character labels, and a few outside labels (after = 75%) run 1-2px past the track.
all.dynamic: Confirmed example: q2 $270K, Q7 7,500, spend $37,500, share 15%. Today is $3,400 at 8.5% of a $40K scale (about 48px at 1280), but the label needs about 76px, so it is clipped. Worst case: under-$10k tier, Q7 4,000, spend $75K, share 15%: '$800' forced into an 8px bar. Correction to the auditor: spend $75K with goal $22,100 at 27.6% is about 155px at 1280 and fits; it clips only at about 320px.
all.suggested_fix: Put the label inside only when the bar is wider than the measured label plus padding. Otherwise place it right after the bar, or after the dashed line when there is room, or else just left of the line. Reproduce through the quiz (Q2 $10k-35k/mo, Q7 5,001-10,000, Q7B $25k-50k, Q7C under 25%) at 1280 and 320, since no DevResults scenario covers it.
all.verifier_note: The defect is real (independent simulation). Counts recomputed with a width check, and the second example corrected (it fits at desktop).

all.dynamic: Scenario 'capped' (DevResults.jsx:165: q2=270000, q7=4000, q8=400, q11=62500, plg). Opt-in is 10% and RPS $13.02, both red, so the headline renders "toward $36.88 and add $125K/month…" above Block 5's "still $122,500 short".

all.requirement: Every red card should show a real gap between today and the goal (edge cases handled).
all.source: Task step 3; calculator loop order close->lead->optIn->rps
all.evidence: calculator.js:242-265; backendValues.js:10-16 (Q2 brackets only, max 4,500,000), 17-27 resolveInputs (q2 = Q2[answers.q2a], no manual entry); validation.js:68 (q11 > q2 check); QuizFlow.jsx:487-491 ('Keep my answers' clamps q11 to q2)
all.detail: The auditor's case cannot happen through the quiz. For RPS to never be raised, the first x1.1 opt-in step would have to add $1.5M on its own, which needs list revenue q11 of at least $15M. But q11 can never exceed q2: it is rejected, or clamped to q2 by 'Keep my answers', and q2 comes only from brackets with a $4.5M maximum. So that step adds at most $450K, the loop always reaches RPS, and RPS always gets at least one raise. Lead and close are raised first in every pass, and opt-in is raised before revenue can change, so no red card can have goal == current. The '$13 -> $13' result only appears with a hand-written input (q2 $40M) that the quiz cannot produce.
all.dynamic: Node with the auditor's input still gives rps $13 -> $13, but that input breaks the q2 bracket cap. With the maximum reachable q11 ($4.5M), the first opt-in step adds $450K < $1.5M, so RPS is always raised.
all.verifier_note: Refuted. The edge case is unreachable because Q2 has no manual entry and q11 is clamped to q2.

all.requirement: Tap (touch) a pillar to highlight it and show the 'We score this one together, live.' bubble
all.evidence: TheCatch.jsx:111-115 focusProps = { onMouseEnter: setFocus(i), onMouseLeave: setFocus(null), onClick: setFocus(f => f === i ? null : i) }; :216-220 bubble only when focus === i; package.json react ^18.3.1
all.detail: Traced through React 18 event handling. On a touch tap, Chrome fires compatibility mouseover (React onMouseEnter, focus = i) and then click. The toggle sees f === i and sets null. React keeps update order, so the final state is null: the first tap on any pillar only flashes. Tapping a different pillar repeats this, and only a second tap on the same pillar sticks. The same handler also hurts desktop: clicking a pillar you are already hovering clears its highlight and bubble. iOS Safari may suppress the click after a hover change, so it could work there. This comes from reading the code; it has not been seen in a browser.
all.suggested_fix: Use onPointerEnter/onPointerLeave guarded by e.pointerType === 'mouse' for hover. Make onClick a toggle only for non-mouse pointers (remember the last pointerType), or have it set focus to i without toggling for mouse. Check in mobile emulation with touch at 375px on ?results=fixture: one tap on PILLAR 02's total should keep the highlight and the bubble.
all.verifier_note: Status changed from needs_decision to wrong. Nobody needs to decide anything; the event sequence plus the toggle gives a deterministic final null on Chromium touch. Browser confirmation still recommended. Desktop click-clears effect added.
